title: Two Sum
problemStatement: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, write a function `twoSum(nums, target)` that returns the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`. You may assume exactly one solution exists and you may not use the same element twice.
description: The answer can be returned in any order. Exactly one valid pair always exists.
constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
-10^9 <= target <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)
inputFormat: An array of integers and an integer target.
explanation: Store each value with its index in a hash map. For each number, check whether target - number is already in the map.

title: Move Zeroes
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, write a function `moveZeroes(nums)` that moves all zeroes to the end of the array while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements. Return the modified array.
description: You must preserve the relative order of non-zero elements.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
outputFormat: The same array with all zeroes moved to the end.

examples.explanation: Non-zero elements 1, 3, 12 keep their order and zeroes move to the end.
All zeroes stay at the end.

explanation: Use a write pointer. Copy every non-zero element forward, then fill the remaining positions with zeroes.

title: Valid Parentheses
problemStatement: Given a string `s` containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', write a function `isValidParentheses(s)` that returns true if the brackets are correctly balanced and closed in the correct order, and false otherwise.
description: An input string is valid if every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket of the same type in the correct order.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^4
s consists only of the characters (){}[]
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)

examples.explanation: Each opening bracket is closed by its matching pair in order.
The opening ( is closed by ] which does not match.

explanation: Use a stack. Push opening brackets and pop when a matching closing bracket is found. The string is valid if the stack is empty at the end.
